html:
SMTO-SKL-0124 — Your Slack connection isn't a member of that channel

GUID: b024a530-81c5-5a5e-a765-055a132f0aa4
Slug: slack-not-in-channel
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack refused because the account or bot SMTO uses isn't in the channel you asked about. Slack didn't carry out the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Slack, open the channel and add the Slack app SMTO uses, or join it with the account you connected. Slack only lets members read or post there, and SMTO never joins channels by itself.
  2. If you can't add it, ask the channel's owner or your Slack workspace admin to add it. Private channels and some workspaces let only owners or admins change who's a member.
  3. Or ask the Agent to list the Slack channels you've joined and choose one of those. A channel the connection already belongs to works without any membership change.
  4. Then ask the Agent for your request again. Slack refused it before doing anything, so it's safe to repeat once membership is sorted out.

What success looks like

  • The Agent can read or post in the channel.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the channel name, to your Slack workspace admin. Don't switch to a different Slack account just to reach the channel.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned not_in_channel: the selected workspace principal (user or bot) is not a member of the target conversation.

What this means

  • Slack returns the not_in_channel API reason. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns the not_in_channel API reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact channel and selected principal's membership.

How to fix it

  • Have the bot user or connected user join the channel_id in Slack (SMTO never changes membership), or pick a conversation from slack.conversations with membership "joined". A bot can post to public channels without joining only if chat:write.public was explicitly granted.
  • Ask the workspace owner to grant the selected principal membership, or select a conversation it already has access to.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended principal has authorized membership or the task uses an accessible conversation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
